key_insight: Early pregnancy HbA1c showed only modest ability to predict later gestational diabetes, with better use as a rough screening aid than a stand-alone diagnostic test.
clinical_relevance: In low- and middle-income settings where OGTT is hard to implement, HbA1c may help triage women for follow-up, but it should not replace confirmatory testing.
method: Multisite prospective cohort of 10,918 pregnancies enrolled before 20 weeks in Kenya, India, Pakistan, and Zambia
Early pregnancy HbA1c was measured at enrollment and compared with later OGTT-based GDM diagnosis
Regression and ROC/AUC analyses assessed prediction and links to adverse pregnancy outcomes
evidence_signal: HbA1c alone had an AUC of 0.65 for predicting GDM; a 5.4% cutoff had limited sensitivity and specificity, and two-threshold rule-out/rule-in cutoffs improved triage behavior but remained imperfect.
watch_item: Performance was only moderate and site-specific implementation may vary, so HbA1c should be used cautiously alongside clinical context and confirmatory OGTT when feasible.
paper_title: Early Pregnancy Glycosylated Hemoglobin in Relation to Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: Evidence from a Multisite Low- and Middle-Income Countries Cohort
